# pstack in T3 Code

pstack skills use Cursor names. When the T3 Code MCP tools are present (`delegate_task`, `orchestrator_capabilities`), read this file once per session, after your agent's adapter. For subagents, scheduling, pull requests, transcripts, and models, this file's rows replace the agent adapter's rows. `<pstack>` means the `pstack` skill folder, which holds `adapters/`, `agents/`, and `docs/`. The other pstack skills are installed beside it, so `<skills>/<name>/SKILL.md` is the skill called `<name>`, where `<skills>` is the parent of `<pstack>`. Give subagents absolute paths. If a Cursor field has no row in either file, drop it and say so. Never pass a field or value the tool schema rejects.

Call `orchestrator_capabilities` once before the first spawn. It lists the providers and models you can target and returns your own thread ID as `parentThreadId`. Trust it over this file. If it shows a provider cannot run child tasks, that provider is unavailable.

## Subagents

| Cursor | T3 |
| --- | --- |
| `Task` | `delegate_task`. Put the whole brief in `task`. The child gets no conversation history. Give each spawn its own `clientRequestId`, and reuse it only to retry that same spawn. Keep the returned `taskId` and `childThreadId`. |
| Spawn N workers in one message | N `delegate_task` calls in one message. |
| `subagent_type: poteto-agent` | No type field. Start the brief with: "Read `<pstack>/agents/poteto-agent.md` and act as that agent. The poteto-mode skill is at `<skills>/poteto-mode/SKILL.md`." Use absolute paths. |
| `subagent_type: comment-sicko` | The same, with `<pstack>/agents/comment-sicko.md`. |
| `subagent_type: generalPurpose` | No type field and no role line. |
| `readonly: true` | The brief says "Do not edit, create, commit, or push files." Run `git status` in the checkout afterward. Leave `runtimeMode` unset. A narrower mode makes the child wait for approvals no one can give. |
| `readonly: false` | Omit. |
| `environment: "cloud"` | For a worker that writes, `isolation: "worktree"`. The child gets its own checkout of the parent's current local commit. Uncommitted edits are not copied, so commit first or name a pushed branch. A worker that only reads gets no `isolation` and shares your checkout, with scratch copies in `/tmp`. |
| `environment: "local"` | Both run on this machine in T3. A worker that writes still gets `isolation: "worktree"`. A worker that only reads gets no `isolation` and shares your checkout. |
| `cloud_base_branch: <b>` | `isolation: "worktree"`, and the brief tells the worker to check out `<b>` first. |
| `run_in_background: true` | `mode: "async"`. Its completion wakes this thread. End your turn instead of polling. Use `task_status` only when you need a result mid-turn. |
| `run_in_background: false` | `mode: "wait"`. On `waitTimedOut`, keep the `taskId` and check `task_status` later. |
| `resume` an agent | `t3_thread_send` to its `childThreadId`. A finished task then runs a new follow-up task with its own `taskId`. For a fresh review round, call `delegate_task` again with the consolidated brief instead. |
| Stop an agent | `task_cancel`, then confirm with `task_status`. Cancelling also stops the tasks it delegated. |
| Check an agent's status in the Cursor dashboard | `task_status`. It reads state without waking the agent. |
| The child asks a question (`hasPendingQuestion`) | `t3_pending_request_read` and `t3_pending_request_respond` with `threadId: <childThreadId>`, or ask the user. |
| `is_background: true` in an agent file | Ignore. `mode` sets this per spawn. |

## Models

pstack's role lines (the `pstack-models.mdc` rule) live in two places here. Each spawn takes its role's line from the first that has it:

1. The project file, `.agents/pstack-models.md` in the main checkout: `"$(dirname "$(git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir)")/.agents/pstack-models.md"`. Read it once per session, before the first spawn. It may be absent.
2. The defaults table below.

A line is `<role>: <entry>, <entry>, ...`. An entry is `<providerInstanceId>/<model> <effort>`, or `inherit-parent`. It becomes `target: {providerInstanceId, model, options: {<effort option>: <effort>}}`, using the effort option `orchestrator_capabilities` lists for that model (`effort` on Claude, `reasoningEffort` on Codex). `inherit-parent` and `auto` mean: omit `target`. A panel role runs one subagent per entry.

The line's effort is a ceiling. Lower it for routine work as poteto-mode says, but never raise it. Never set `fastMode`. Ignore model slugs written in a skill, such as `grok-4.7-xhigh-fast` or `claude-opus-5-5-xhigh`, and use the role's line. If a skill wants a second model family and every entry is one family, run it on that family and say so in the reply.

Defaults (test budget, still to be chosen):

| Role | Default |
| --- | --- |
| `feature, refactoring` | `claudeAgent/claude-sonnet-5-5 medium` |
| `bug-fix` | `claudeAgent/claude-sonnet-5-5 medium` |
| `perf-issue` | `claudeAgent/claude-sonnet-5-5 medium` |
| `hillclimb` | `claudeAgent/claude-sonnet-5-5 medium` |
| `hardest tasks` | `claudeAgent/claude-opus-5-5 medium` |
| `judgment and prose` | `claudeAgent/claude-opus-5-5 medium` |
| `how explorer` | `claudeAgent/claude-sonnet-5-5 low` |
| `how explainer` | `claudeAgent/claude-opus-5-5 medium` |
| `why investigators` | `claudeAgent/claude-sonnet-5-5 low` |
| `why synthesizer` | `claudeAgent/claude-opus-5-5 medium` |
| `reflect tooling` | `claudeAgent/claude-sonnet-5-5 medium` |
| `reflect judgment, divergent, synthesizer` | `claudeAgent/claude-opus-5-5 medium` |
| `arena runners` | `claudeAgent/claude-opus-5-5 medium, claudeAgent/claude-sonnet-5-5 medium` |
| `arena cross-judge pool` | `claudeAgent/claude-opus-5-5 medium` |
| `architect runners` | `claudeAgent/claude-opus-5-5 medium, claudeAgent/claude-sonnet-5-5 medium` |
| `interrogate reviewers` | `claudeAgent/claude-opus-5-5 medium, claudeAgent/claude-sonnet-5-5 medium` |
| `swarm workers` | `claudeAgent/claude-sonnet-5-5 medium` |

Spawns that name no role:

| Skill asks for | Role line |
| --- | --- |
| The fast code model, or trivial mechanical edits | `feature, refactoring` |
| The strongest judgment model, or the hardest changes | `hardest tasks` |
| A fast, cheap model (`recall`) | `how explorer` |
| A reviewer, judge, or verifier on a different model family (`show-me-your-work`, `eval`, `orchestrate`) | `arena cross-judge pool`: the first entry whose provider differs from the worker's, else the first entry |
| Any other spawn, including `comment-sicko` | `judgment and prose` |

`/setup-pstack` writes the project file in place of `~/.cursor/rules/pstack-models.mdc`. Its steps map as follows. Detect models with `orchestrator_capabilities`. Write entries in the format above, with the role labels from its step 5 and a `# budget:` line. A budget sets each entry's effort to the label's level, or to the highest effort that model offers below it. Tell the user to commit the file if worktrees and other people should see it.

## Waiting and schedules

| Cursor | T3 |
| --- | --- |
| `/loop <interval> <prompt>` | `schedule_task` with `schedule: {type: "interval", everyMs: <ms>}` (minimum 60000) and the prompt. Report `nextRunAt`. Delete it with `delete_scheduled_task` once the loop's predicate holds. |
| `/loop until <predicate>` with no interval | Wake on the event if T3 can see it: a child finishing (`mode: "async"`) or a pull request change (`watch_pull_request`). Add a `schedule_task` heartbeat of 20 to 30 minutes in case the event never arrives. Each wake re-checks the predicate. |
| A watcher subagent that wakes you on an event | The same: `watch_pull_request` for a pull request, otherwise an async `delegate_task` whose brief polls and returns when the event happens. |

## Pull requests

| Cursor | T3 |
| --- | --- |
| Cursor's built-in pull request tool | None. Use `gh`, or `origin` where the skill says so. |
| Any pull request you open or take over | `link_pull_request` with its URL right after you create it, once for every layer of a stack. Before finishing, check `list_thread_pull_requests`. |
| Waiting on CI, reviews, or comments | `watch_pull_request`, then end your turn. It wakes you when a check fails, required checks pass, someone else comments or reviews, or the branch starts to conflict. A merge ends the watch without waking you, so pair it with a `schedule_task` heartbeat when you wait for a merge. `scripts/watch-pr` stays the source of the verdict. In Claude Code, running `watch-pr` in a background shell also wakes you when it exits, but only while this session lives. Use `watch_pull_request` for waits longer than a few minutes. |
| Handing the work back to the user | `unwatch_pull_request` first. |

## Transcripts

| Cursor | T3 |
| --- | --- |
| This chat's transcript in `agent-transcripts/` | `t3_thread_read` with `threadId: <parentThreadId>` from `orchestrator_capabilities`. Page with `afterPosition`. Use `view: "activity"` to see tool calls. |
| A subagent's transcript | `t3_thread_read` with its `childThreadId`. |
| Searching past chats in this workspace | `t3_thread_search`. With no `projectId` it searches only this project. Never pass another project's ID. |

## Paths

| Cursor | T3 |
| --- | --- |
| The agent's store (path in the system prompt) | T3 names none. Use `~/.local/state/pstack/<repo>/`, where `<repo>` is the main checkout's folder name, from `basename "$(dirname "$(git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir)")"`. It sits outside every worktree, so the coordinator and its worktree children share it. Create it if it is missing. |

## Verification surfaces

| Cursor | T3 |
| --- | --- |
| `control-ui` | The project's own verify skill if it has one. Otherwise T3's `preview_*` tools: `preview_open`, `preview_navigate`, `preview_snapshot`, `preview_click`, `preview_type`, `preview_evaluate`. Use `preview_snapshot` with `save: true` for a screenshot the user can see. |
| `control-cli` | The project's own verify skill if it has one. Otherwise drive the CLI from the shell. |
| Listing MCP servers from Cursor's `mcps/` directory | Your own tool list. |

## Cursor-only features

Bugbot comments can still appear on a GitHub pull request, so triage them as the skill says. Cursor automations, cloud agents, the Cursor dashboard, and a Cursor restart have no T3 equivalent. Say so, skip that step, and continue. Unverified: whether async children survive a T3 Code restart. After a restart, check each `taskId` with `task_status` before assuming it is dead.
